script: セイバールート十三日目-11
title: セイバールート十三日目-11

pages.ja:
一人、目を覚ました。
体調が回復しても、セイバーは定期的に睡眠を取らなくてはならない。
あれから部屋に戻ってすぐにセイバーは眠り、俺も彼女を安心させる為に床についた。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
I awaken alone.

Even with her health restored, Saber still needs to sleep at regular intervals.

She fell asleep as soon as we returned to the room, and I went to bed as well to put her mind at ease.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I wake up alone.
Even if she has recovered, Saber still has to sleep periodically.
Saber went to bed right away after that, and I went to bed too to relieve Saber.

pages.ja:
それが一時間前の話だ。
時刻は十二時過ぎ。……この時間なら、セイバーと遠坂に見つかる事なく外に出られる。
pages.jaRuby:
それが一時間前の話だ。
時刻は十二時過ぎ。……この時間なら、セイバーと遠坂に見つかる事なく外に出られる。
pages.en:
That was an hour ago.

It is past midnight now. At this hour, I should be able to slip outside without Saber or Tohsaka noticing.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That was an hour ago.
It’s past midnight. …I’ll be able to sneak out without Saber or Tohsaka finding out now.

pages.ja:
物音を立てないように外に出た。
自転車を使おうとも思ったが、それで二人を起こしては面倒だ。
ここは歩いて向かう事にしよう。
pages.jaRuby:

ここは歩いて向かう事にしよう。
pages.en:
I leave the house without making a sound.

I considered taking my bicycle, but waking the two of them would only create trouble.

I will go on foot.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I go out without making a sound.
I thought about using the bicycle, but it’d be a problem if I wake them up by doing so.
I guess I’ll walk there.

pages.ja:
人の気配がしない。
いくら深夜だからといって、この静けさは異常だった。
空気は凍り付き、建物には生気というものが感じられない。
pages.jaRuby:
人の気配がしない。

空気は凍り付き、建物には生気というものが感じられない。
pages.en:
There is no sign of another person anywhere.

Even after midnight, this silence is unnatural.

The air lies frozen, and the buildings seem utterly lifeless.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There’s no one around.
Even if it’s midnight, this silence is abnormal.
The air is frozen and I can’t sense life from any of the buildings.

pages.ja:
反面、足の下、地面の中では、何か黒々としたものが渦巻いているような、矛盾した熱を感じる。
……イリヤに捕まっていた数日の間に、町はどうかしてしまったのか。
なにか、よくない事が起こる兆しが、そこかしこに溢れている気がした。
pages.jaRuby:
反面、足の下、地面の中では、何か黒々としたものが渦巻いているような、矛盾した熱を感じる。
……イリヤに捕まっていた数日の間に、町はどうかしてしまったのか。
なにか、よくない事が起こる兆しが、そこかしこに溢れている気がした。
pages.en:
Yet beneath my feet, deep in the earth, I sense a contradictory heat—as though something black were seething underground.

…Did something happen to the city during the days Illya held me captive?

Everywhere I look, the night seems thick with omens of something terrible to come.
pages.mirrorMoon:
On the other hand, I feel a contradictory heat under the road as if there’s a whirlpool of something black.
…Has something happened to the town in the few days I was held at Illya’s place?
It feels like ill omens are everywhere.

pages.ja:
「………………気のせい、じゃないよな」
ふと、遠くのお山を見上げる。
町から離れた柳洞寺は、ここから見れば黒い塊にしか見えなかった。
ただ、それが。
夜気にゆられて、どくん、と鳴動するように見えた。
pages.jaRuby:
「………………気のせい、じゃないよな」
ふと、遠くのお山を見上げる。
町から離れた柳洞寺は、ここから見れば黒い塊にしか見えなかった。
ただ、それが。
夜気にゆられて、どくん、と鳴動するように見えた。
pages.en:
“………………I’m not imagining it.”

I happen to glance toward the distant mountain.

From here, Ryuudou Temple is nothing more than a black mass beyond the city.

But that mass—

seems to stir in the night air with the pulse of a vast, beating heart.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…It’s not just me.”
I look up at the mountain in the distance.
The Ryuudou Temple which is far away from the city just looks like a black lump from here.
It’s just that…
It seems like it’s throbbing along with the night wind.

pages.ja:
暗い川を渡って、新都へ歩いていく。
「
そうか。あれから、もう十日経ってるのか」
あの日。
初めてセイバーと出逢った夜、遠坂と三人でこの橋を歩いた事が、随分と昔に感じられた。
pages.jaRuby:

あの日。
初めてセイバーと出逢った夜、遠坂と三人でこの橋を歩いた事が、随分と昔に感じられた。
pages.en:
I cross the dark river and walk on toward the new city.

“—I see. It’s already been ten days.”

That night.

The first night I met Saber, when the three of us crossed this bridge together, feels impossibly distant now.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I cross the dark river and walk to Shinto.
“
That’s right. It’s already been ten days since then.”
That day.
That night I first met Saber and walked on this bridge with Tohsaka seems like so long ago.

pages.ja:
教会が見える。
『今まで、一度も行った事はない』
そう遠坂に答えたものの、あの教会とは少なからず縁があった。
なにしろ、本当なら俺はあの教会に預けられ、どこぞの養子縁組に組み込まれた筈なんだから。
pages.jaRuby:
教会が見える。
『今まで、一度も行った事はない』
そう遠坂に答えたものの、あの教会とは少なからず縁があった。
なにしろ、本当なら俺はあの教会に預けられ、どこぞの養子縁組に組み込まれた筈なんだから。
pages.en:
—The church comes into view.

*I’ve never been there before.*

That is what I told Tohsaka, but the church and I do share a connection.

After all, I was supposed to be entrusted to its care and placed with some adoptive family.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I see the church.
“I’ve never been to the church.”
Even though I told Tohsaka that, I do have a connection to this church.
I was supposed to be entrusted to the church and adopted somewhere later.

pages.ja: 「……衛宮の家か、あの教会か。思えば、とんでもない分かれ道だったんだな」
pages.jaRuby: 「……衛宮の家か、あの教会か。思えば、とんでもない分かれ道だったんだな」
pages.en: “…The Emiya home or that church. When I think about it, that was one hell of a fork in the road.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…The Emiya household or the church. Come to think of it, it was a big turning point.”

pages.ja:
十年前。
あの病室にいた子供たちはみんな孤児で、一時的に教会に預けられた。
俺はそんな孤児たちの中でただ一人、病室から養子として貰われた。
pages.jaRuby:
十年前。
あの病室にいた子供たちはみんな孤児で、一時的に教会に預けられた。
俺はそんな孤児たちの中でただ一人、病室から養子として貰われた。
pages.en:
Ten years ago, every child in that hospital room had been orphaned, and all of us were temporarily placed in the church’s care.

I was the only one taken straight from the hospital and adopted.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Ten years ago.
All the children in that hospital were orphans, and they were all temporarily entrusted to the church.
I was the only one of them adopted from the hospital.

pages.ja:
だからだろう。
なんだか申し訳なくって、無意識にあの教会を避け続けたのは。
十一日前の夜、教会に行くのは初めてだ、と遠坂に答えたのはそういう訳だった。
pages.jaRuby:
だからだろう。
なんだか申し訳なくって、無意識にあの教会を避け続けたのは。
十一日前の夜、教会に行くのは初めてだ、と遠坂に答えたのはそういう訳だった。
pages.en:
That must be why.

Some part of me felt guilty, and I kept avoiding the church without even realizing it.

That was why, eleven nights ago, I told Tohsaka I had never been there before.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That must be why.
I felt kind of guilty and unconsciously avoided the church.
That’s why I told Tohsaka it was my first time visiting the church on the night eleven days ago.

pages.ja:
教会に明かりは点いていた。
……あの神父は苦手だが、あいつには訊かなければならない事がある。
「
さあ、行くぞ」
ふう、と軽く深呼吸をして、重苦しい扉に手をかけた。
pages.jaRuby:

「
さあ、行くぞ」
ふう、と軽く深呼吸をして、重苦しい扉に手をかけた。
pages.en:
Lights are burning inside the church.

…I do not like that priest, but there are things I have to ask him.

“—All right. Here goes.”

I take a quiet breath and place my hand against the ponderous door.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The lights in the church are still on.
…I don’t like that priest, but there’s something I need to ask him.
“
Well, let’s go.”
I take a deep breath and go through the heavy doors.

pages.ja:
「言峰神父、いるか」
声をかけながら歩を進める。
礼拝堂に人の気配はない。
明かりは点いているものの、こう無闇に広くて静かだと、下手な暗闇より緊張する。
pages.jaRuby:
「言峰神父、いるか」
声をかけながら歩を進める。
礼拝堂に人の気配はない。
明かりは点いているものの、こう無闇に広くて静かだと、下手な暗闇より緊張する。
pages.en:
“Father Kotomine? Are you here?”

I call out as I venture inside.

There is no one in the chapel.

The lights are on, but in a space this needlessly vast and silent, I feel more exposed than I would in darkness.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Priest Kotomine, are you here?”
I keep on walking while I call out.
I can’t sense anyone in the chapel.
Even though the lights are on, it’s so big and quiet that I feel more afraid than I would in complete darkness.

pages.ja:
「おい。誰かいないのか」
……返事はない。
これ以上奥に行くわけにもいかないし、今夜は諦めて帰るべきなのか
pages.jaRuby:
「おい。誰かいないのか」
……返事はない。
これ以上奥に行くわけにもいかないし、今夜は諦めて帰るべきなのか
pages.en:
“Hey. Is anybody here?”

…No answer.

I cannot very well wander any farther into the building. Maybe I should give up for tonight and go home—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey, is anyone here?”
…There’s no reply.
I can’t go in any farther, so maybe I should give up and go home for tonight

pages.ja:
「っ……！」
咄嗟に物音へと振り返る。
「衛宮士郎か。こんな時間に何の用だ」
pages.jaRuby:
「っ……！」
咄嗟に物音へと振り返る。
「衛宮士郎か。こんな時間に何の用だ」
pages.en:
“—!”

I whirl toward the sudden sound.

“Shirou Emiya. What brings you here at this hour?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…!”
I instantly turn toward the sound.
“So, it is Emiya Shirou. What are you doing here at this time?”

pages.ja:
「
」
突然の対面で、うまい言葉が見つからない。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
突然の対面で、うまい言葉が見つからない。
pages.en:
“—”

Faced with him so abruptly, I cannot find the right words.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
The sudden encounter leaves me speechless.

pages.ja:
「夜も更けた。後は眠るだけだったのだが
その顔では懺悔の真似事でもしたかったと見えるな、衛宮士郎」
言峰はつまらなげに言って、やってきた扉へと踵を返す。
pages.jaRuby:
「夜も更けた。後は眠るだけだったのだが
その顔では懺悔の真似事でもしたかったと見えるな、衛宮士郎」
言峰はつまらなげに言って、やってきた扉へと踵を返す。
pages.en:
“The hour is late, and I had nothing left to do but sleep. Yet by that expression, I take it you came hoping to make some pale imitation of a confession, Shirou Emiya.”

Kotomine delivers the remark without interest, then turns back toward the door through which he entered.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It is late. I was going to sleep
but your expression suggests that you seek confession here.”
Kotomine says so and returns to the door he emerged from.

pages.ja:
「あ
いや、待ってくれ。その、アンタに訊きたい事があって来た」
「そんな事は判っている。時間外だからといって、訪れた者を追い返す事などせん」
言って、言峰は奥に通じる扉を開けた。
pages.jaRuby:
「あ
いや、待ってくれ。その、アンタに訊きたい事があって来た」
「そんな事は判っている。時間外だからといって、訪れた者を追い返す事などせん」
言って、言峰は奥に通じる扉を開けた。
pages.en:
“Ah—no, wait. I came because there’s something I need to ask you.”

“That much is obvious. I would hardly turn away a visitor simply because he arrived outside the appointed hours.”

With that, Kotomine opens a door leading deeper into the church.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh
no, wait. Um, I had something I wanted to ask you.”
“I know. I will not turn anyone away even if they come at odd hours.”
So saying, Kotomine opens the door to the back of the chapel.

pages.ja:
「ついてこい。話といっても聖杯戦争の件だろう。そんな血生臭い話をここでする訳にもいかん」
こっちの返事も待たず、言峰は奥へ消えていった。
pages.jaRuby:
「ついてこい。話といっても聖杯戦争の件だろう。そんな血生臭い話をここでする訳にもいかん」
こっちの返事も待たず、言峰は奥へ消えていった。
pages.en:
“Follow me. You have come to discuss the Holy Grail War, I presume. The chapel is no place for so bloody a subject.”

Without waiting for my answer, Kotomine disappears through the doorway.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Follow me. I’m sure it has to do with the Holy Grail War. I cannot have us talk about such bloody subjects here.”
Kotomine disappears into the back without waiting for my reply.

pages.ja:
「
っ」
ここまで来たんだ、何もせずには帰れない。
言峰の雰囲気に威圧されないよう気合いを入れ直して、教会の奥へと向かった。
pages.jaRuby:
「
っ」
ここまで来たんだ、何もせずには帰れない。
言峰の雰囲気に威圧されないよう気合いを入れ直して、教会の奥へと向かった。
pages.en:
“—”

I have come this far. I cannot leave without accomplishing anything.

Steeling myself against the weight of Kotomine’s presence, I follow him into the depths of the church.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
!”
I’ve come this far, so I can’t go back empty-handed.
I renew my determination not to be intimidated by Kotomine and follow him.

pages.ja:
「わ
外も凄かったけど、中も凝ってるっていうか……」
中庭、だろうか。
言峰一人が住むにはあまりにも立派な庭園と渡り廊下が広がっている。
pages.jaRuby:
「わ
外も凄かったけど、中も凝ってるっていうか……」
中庭、だろうか。
言峰一人が住むにはあまりにも立派な庭園と渡り廊下が広がっている。
pages.en:
“Whoa—the outside was impressive enough, but this place is something else…”

Is this a courtyard?

An elaborate garden and covered walkway stretch before me, far grander than anything one man could need.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wow
the outside was brilliant, but the inside is exquisite as well…”
Is this a courtyard?
There’s a park and passageway that seems too elegant for Kotomine to live in alone.

pages.ja:
「なにをしている。話をするのならこちらに来い」
神父は何個めかの曲がり角を進んでいく。
pages.jaRuby:
「なにをしている。話をするのならこちらに来い」
神父は何個めかの曲がり角を進んでいく。
pages.en:
“What are you doing? If you mean to talk, come this way.”

The priest vanishes around yet another corner.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What are you doing? Come here if you have something to talk about.”
The priest turns yet another corner.

pages.ja:
「……くそ、ホントにまったなしなんだな、アイツ」
愚痴をこぼしつつ、言峰の後を追う。
教会はちょっとした迷路で、今は大人しく言峰に従うしかなかった。
pages.jaRuby:
「……くそ、ホントにまったなしなんだな、アイツ」
愚痴をこぼしつつ、言峰の後を追う。
教会はちょっとした迷路で、今は大人しく言峰に従うしかなかった。
pages.en:
“…Damn it. That guy really never waits for anyone.”

Grumbling, I hurry after him.

The church is a small maze, and for now I have no choice but to follow his lead.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Damn, he really doesn’t wait.”
I follow him, complaining.
The church is like a small maze, so I have to follow him obediently.

pages.ja:
「
」
質素な石造りの部屋だった。
あの礼拝堂や中庭の優雅さとはかけ離れたここが、言峰神父の私室らしい。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
質素な石造りの部屋だった。
あの礼拝堂や中庭の優雅さとはかけ離れたここが、言峰神父の私室らしい。
pages.en:
“—”

The room is a bare chamber of stone.

Though entirely unlike the elegance of the chapel and courtyard, it seems to be Father Kotomine’s private quarters.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
It’s a modest room made of stone.
This inelegant room seems to be Kotomine’s.

pages.ja:
「持てなす物のひとつもないが、許せ」
ずっしりとソファーに身を預けながら、神父はそんな事を言う。
pages.jaRuby:
「持てなす物のひとつもないが、許せ」
ずっしりとソファーに身を預けながら、神父はそんな事を言う。
pages.en:
“I have nothing with which to entertain you. Forgive me.”

The priest sinks heavily into a sofa as he speaks.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I am unfortunately out of alcohol. I
“I
have nothing to welcome you with, but forgive me.”
Kotomine says so while sitting down.

pages.ja:
「
」
……微かに匂うのはワインか何かの香りか。
匂いが部屋に染みついているぐらいなんだから、相当の好き者なのだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
……微かに匂うのはワインか何かの香りか。
匂いが部屋に染みついているぐらいなんだから、相当の好き者なのだろう。
pages.en:
“—”

…The faint scent in the air must be wine, or something like it.

If it has seeped this deeply into the room, he must be quite a serious drinker.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
…Is this the faint smell of wine?
He must really like it if the smell is lingering in this room.

pages.ja:
「どうした、話があるのではなかったか。そこで惚けられていても迷惑だが」
「
だ、誰も惚けてなんかいないっ！ この部屋が意外だったから驚いていただけで、すぐに用件を済ませて帰る……！」
pages.jaRuby:
「どうした、話があるのではなかったか。そこで惚けられていても迷惑だが」
「
だ、誰も惚けてなんかいないっ！ この部屋が意外だったから驚いていただけで、すぐに用件を済ませて帰る……！」
pages.en:
“Well? Did you not have something to discuss? Standing there in a stupor is of little use to either of us.”

“I-I’m not in a stupor! This room wasn’t what I expected, that’s all. I’ll ask what I came to ask and be on my way…!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What? Did you not have something to talk to me about? It is bothersome if you just stand there dumbfounded.”
“I-I’m not dumbfounded! I was just surprised by this room, and I’ll go home right away once I’m done with my business…!”

pages.ja:
「それはなにより。私も子供に付き合うほど暇ではない。
質問は手短かにして貰おう」
「っ…………」
……やはりこの男は苦手だ。
心を見透かされているようで、正面から対峙すると気圧されてしまう。
pages.jaRuby:
「それはなにより。私も子供に付き合うほど暇ではない。

「っ…………」
……やはりこの男は苦手だ。
心を見透かされているようで、正面から対峙すると気圧されてしまう。
pages.en:
“Good. I have no leisure to indulge a child.

“Keep your questions brief.”

“…………”

…I knew it. I cannot stand this man.

It feels as though he can see straight through me, and facing him head-on leaves me overwhelmed.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Good. I do not have enough leisure time to socialize with children either.
Keep your questions concise.”
“…!”
…As expected, I hate this guy.
It feels like he can read my mind, and I feel intimidated when I talk to him.

pages.ja: 「それで、話はなんだ衛宮士郎。一応、教えられる事は全て教えたつもりだが」
pages.jaRuby: 「それで、話はなんだ衛宮士郎。一応、教えられる事は全て教えたつもりだが」
pages.en: “Then what is it, Shirou Emiya? I believe I have already told you everything I am at liberty to teach.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “So, what is it that you want to talk about, Emiya Shirou? I believe I have already told you everything I can.”

pages.ja:
「……嘘つけ、アンタは知ってた筈だ。
親父がセイバーのマスターだったこと、最後に聖杯を壊しちまったことを。アンタは聖杯を管理している監督役なんだからな……！」
pages.jaRuby:
「……嘘つけ、アンタは知ってた筈だ。
親父がセイバーのマスターだったこと、最後に聖杯を壊しちまったことを。アンタは聖杯を管理している監督役なんだからな……！」
pages.en:
“…Liar. You knew.

連中は何代かに渡って“万能の釜”を再現する儀式を模索し、二百年前にそれを完成させた。
それが一度目の聖杯戦争
人工物に過ぎない聖杯に“万能の釜”を降霊させ、道を開こうとした儀式だった」
pages.en:
“They were the three founding families: the Einzberns, the Makiri, and the Tohsakas.

“For generations, they sought a ritual that would reproduce the almighty cauldron. Two hundred years ago, they completed it.

“That was the first Holy Grail War—a ritual meant to summon the almighty cauldron into an artificial Grail and open the path to it.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“They were the three families: Einzbern, Makiri, and Tohsaka.
They spent many generations researching the ritual to reproduce the omnipotent vessel and completed it two hundred years ago.
That was the first Holy Grail War
the ritual that summoned the omnipotent vessel to the artificial Holy Grail to open up the path.”

pages.ja: 「アインツベルン……？ それって、イリヤの家の事か？」
pages.jaRuby: 「アインツベルン……？ それって、イリヤの家の事か？」
pages.en: “Einzbern…? You mean Illya’s family?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Einzbern…? You mean, Illya’s family?”

pages.ja:
「そうだ。アインツベルンはラインの黄金とやらの伝承に長けていてな。こと、聖杯の模造品を作る技術は神業だった。
だがそれだけでは聖杯を呼び出す事はできん。
相応しい土地と、強力な呪縛が必要となる。
それらを提供したのが遠坂とマキリだ」
pages.jaRuby:
「そうだ。アインツベルンはラインの黄金とやらの伝承に長けていてな。こと、聖杯の模造品を作る技術は神業だった。

pages.en:
“Indeed. The Einzberns were well versed in the tradition of the Rhinegold. Their skill at crafting an imitation of the Holy Grail was nothing short of divine.

“But that alone could not summon the Grail.

“They required suitable land and a powerful binding.

“The Tohsakas and the Makiri provided them.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes. The Einzberns specialized in ‘the golden rule of the line’. They were the best suited to make an imitation of the Holy Grail.
But they cannot summon the Holy Grail with just that.
They need a suitable land and a strong curse.
The ones who provided these were the Tohsaka and the Makiri.”

pages.ja:
「当時、教会と魔術協会は係争の真っ最中だったからな。 儀式には教会の目が届かない極東の地が選ばれた。
アインツベルンはそれを見越して遠坂を仲間に引き入れたのだろう。遠坂はここ一帯の霊地の持ち主であり、その師は降霊術の大家だった。
アインツベルンとしては、遠坂なくして聖杯召喚は不可能だった」

pages.en:
“At the time, the Church and the Mage's Association were locked in open conflict. They therefore chose for their ritual a land in the Far East, beyond the Church's eyes.

“No doubt the Einzberns brought the Tohsakas into their scheme with that in mind. The Tohsakas owned the spiritual land throughout this region, and their master was a renowned practitioner of spirit evocation.

“Without the Tohsakas, the Einzberns could not have summoned the Grail.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“At that time, the Church and the Magic Association were in the middle of a bloody war. A far eastern land was chosen as the place for the ritual.
Einzbern must have invited Tohsaka in because Tohsaka was in charge of the land around here and their master was a master of summoning.
For Einzbern, the summoning of the Holy Grail would be impossible without the help of Tohsaka.”

pages.ja:
「だが、二つの家だけでは容易に裏切りが起きてしまう。
事は三すくみにすべきだ、と考えたのか、遠坂はマキリの家系にもこの話を持ち込んだ。
マキリも長い年月を持つ名門でな。
こと使い魔に関しては優れた技法を持っていた。サーヴァントを縛る令呪を作り上げたのもマキリだ」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“But with only two families, betrayal would have come too easily.

“Perhaps deciding the matter required a three-way deadlock, the Tohsakas extended the proposal to the Makiri bloodline as well.

“The Makiri were another distinguished house of ancient lineage.

“Their techniques concerning familiars were especially accomplished. It was the Makiri who devised the Command Spells that bind the Servants.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But betrayal could easily occur with two families involved.
They must have thought three should be involved as they also brought in the Makiri family.
The Makiris are a family with history as well.
They were the family most skilled with familiars. It was they that came up with the Command Spell to bind the Servants.”

pages.ja:
「……そうして連中は聖杯召喚に一致団結した訳だが、いざ成功してみれば残ったのは潰し合いだ。
一度目の聖杯の降霊は、連中が戦っている間に終わってしまったらしいな。
そうして代を重ね、聖杯戦争というルールを作り、カタチだけはもとの協力関係に戻った」

pages.en:
“…And so the families united to summon the Grail. But once they succeeded, they turned on one another.

“The first summoning of the Holy Grail apparently ended while they were still fighting.

“With each succeeding generation, they established the rules of the Holy Grail War and restored the outward form of their original alliance.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…And they worked together to summon the Holy Grail, but when they succeeded, what came after was bloody killing.
The first summoning of the Holy Grail ended while they were busy
killing each other.
fighting.
As generations passed, they made rules called the Holy Grail War and went back to cooperating, at least in form.”

pages.ja:
「遠坂はこの土地とサーヴァントを形作るシステムを提供し、マキリはサーヴァントを縛る令呪を提供した。
そしてアインツベルンは聖杯が宿る器を用意する。
それが彼らの敷いた協力関係という訳だ」
pages.jaRuby:
「遠坂はこの土地とサーヴァントを形作るシステムを提供し、マキリはサーヴァントを縛る令呪を提供した。
そしてアインツベルンは聖杯が宿る器を用意する。
それが彼らの敷いた協力関係という訳だ」
pages.en:
“The Tohsakas provide this land and the system that gives form to the Servants. The Makiri provide the Command Spells that bind them.

“And the Einzberns prepare the vessel in which the Grail takes residence.

“Such is the arrangement they established.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Tohsaka provided this land and the system to model the Servants, and Makiri provided the Command Spell to bind these Servants.
And Einzbern supplies the vessel for the Holy Grail to dwell in.
That is the cooperation they decided on.”

pages.ja:
……何が愉しいのか、神父は嬉しそうに続ける。
しかし、そうか……聖杯戦争は儀式だって言っていたが、その発案者がイリヤや遠坂の家だったのか。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
…For some reason, the priest seems delighted as he continues.

Still, I see… He called the Holy Grail War a ritual, but it was Illya and Tohsaka’s families that devised it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The priest continues happily as if something pleases him.
But, I see… they say the Holy Grail War is a ritual, but Illya’s family was the original proposer.

pages.ja:
「聖杯を用意したのはアインツベルンだからな。
前回切嗣に裏切られた彼等は、最強の切り札を投入してきた。おそらくアインツベルンの娘が聖杯を持っているのだろう」
pages.jaRuby:
「聖杯を用意したのはアインツベルンだからな。
前回切嗣に裏切られた彼等は、最強の切り札を投入してきた。おそらくアインツベルンの娘が聖杯を持っているのだろう」
pages.en:
“The Einzberns are responsible for providing the Grail.

“Betrayed by Kiritsugu in the last war, they have now committed their greatest trump card. The Einzbern girl is most likely carrying the Grail.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It was the Einzberns that prepared the Holy Grail.
As they were betrayed by Kiritsugu last time, they have thrown in their greatest trump card. The daughter of Einzbern probably holds the Holy Grail.”

pages.ja:
「
？」
イリヤが聖杯を持っている……？
……おかしいな、そんな荷物はなかった筈だが……。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“—?”

Illya is carrying the Grail…?

…That is strange. I do not remember her having any luggage.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
?”
Illya has the Holy Grail…?
…That’s weird. I don’t think she had anything with her…

pages.ja:

だが、解決する手段は聖杯のみだ。それが解ったのなら早々に帰るがいい。
戦いはまだ終わっていない。セイバーもつけずに出歩くのは正気の沙汰ではないぞ」

pages.en:
“Now, are you satisfied? I cannot know what troubles you.

“But only the Grail can provide a solution. Now that you understand, you should return home at once.

“The war is not yet over. Roaming the city without Saber at your side is sheer madness.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well, are you happy now? I do not know what troubles you.
But the only way to solve it is to use the Holy Grail. Now that you know that, go home.
The battle is not yet over. You are crazy to be walking about without having Saber by your side.”

pages.ja:
「余計なお世話だ。まだランサーのマスターが残っている事ぐらい
」
と、待て。
まだ一つ、訊かなければならない事があった。
pages.jaRuby:

」

pages.en:
“That’s none of your business. I know Lancer’s Master is still—”

Wait.

There is one more thing I have to ask him.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That’s none of your business. I know there’s still Lancer’s Master
”
Hold on.
There’s one more thing I need to ask him.

pages.en:
“—Kotomine. You said that when the Grail disappears, the Servants disappear with it.

“You did say that.”

“I did. Is there a problem?”

“Of course there is. I don’t know who he was, but there was an eighth Servant. Saber says he has remained here ever since the last war.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Kotomine. Servants will disappear once the Holy Grail disappears.
That’s what you said, right?”
“Yes. Do you have a problem with that?”
“I do. I don’t know who it is, but there is an eighth Servant. According to Saber, he has remained in this world since the previous war.”

pages.ja:

？」

Perhaps it truly caught him by surprise.

Kotomine stares wide-eyed and mutters that it is absurd.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wha
t?”
It must have been a surprise.
Kotomine opens his eyes and mutters in disbelief.

pages.ja: 「どういう事だ言峰。アンタなら少しは判ると思って来たんだぞ」
pages.jaRuby: 「どういう事だ言峰。アンタなら少しは判ると思って来たんだぞ」
pages.en: “What does it mean, Kotomine? I came because I thought you might at least know that much.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “What’s going on? I came here since I thought you would know.”

pages.ja:
「…………。消えなかったサーヴァントがいる、という事だな。
そう不思議ではあるまい。前回の戦いは、セイバーが聖杯を破壊する事で終わったのだ。
つまりセイバーの他にもう一人、サーヴァントは残っていた」
pages.jaRuby:
「…………。消えなかったサーヴァントがいる、という事だな。

pages.en:
“………… There was a Servant who did not disappear. Is that what you are saying?

“It is hardly inconceivable. The previous war ended when Saber destroyed the Grail.

“Which means that, besides Saber, one other Servant still remained.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…So, you are saying there is a Servant that did not disappear?
It is not that strange. The previous war ended with Saber destroying the Holy Grail.
So in other words, there was still another Servant left.”

pages.ja:
「セイバーは潔く消えたが、そのサーヴァントが現界する事を望んだのなら話は容易い。
ソレは魂を喰らう事で魔力を補い、この十年間生き続けたのだろう」
pages.jaRuby:
「セイバーは潔く消えたが、そのサーヴァントが現界する事を望んだのなら話は容易い。
ソレは魂を喰らう事で魔力を補い、この十年間生き続けたのだろう」
pages.en:
“Saber accepted her disappearance, but if the other Servant wished to remain incarnate, the explanation is simple.

“It may have fed upon souls to replenish its magical energy and survived for the past ten years.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Saber disappeared by her own will, but if a Servant wished to stay, then the answer is simple.
He must have acquired
magical energy
the magical energy he needed
by feeding on souls and lived these past ten years.”

pages.ja:
「
そんなバカな。あいつの気配は異常だった。
あんなのが十年間もいたら、親父だってアンタだって気が付くはずだ」
pages.jaRuby:
「
そんなバカな。あいつの気配は異常だった。
あんなのが十年間もいたら、親父だってアンタだって気が付くはずだ」
pages.en:
“—That’s impossible. His presence was monstrous.

“If something like that had been here for ten years, my old man would have noticed. So would you.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
That’s ridiculous. His presence was absurd.
You or my father certainly would’ve noticed if that thing had been around for ten years.”

pages.ja:
「……分かっている。おそらく匿っている者がいたのだろう。そのサーヴァントのマスターか、もしくは……」
「もしくは、なんだよ」
pages.jaRuby:
「……分かっている。おそらく匿っている者がいたのだろう。そのサーヴァントのマスターか、もしくは……」
「もしくは、なんだよ」
pages.en:
“…I am aware of that. Presumably someone concealed the Servant. Its Master, perhaps. Or else…”

“Or else what?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I know. Someone was probably hiding him. The Servant’s Master, or…”
“Or what?”

pages.ja:
「聖杯戦争を知りながら、マスターの資格を持ち得なかった魔術師だ。
そういった人物には一人心当たりがあるのだが、それもないな。マキリのご老体はとうに隠居している」
納得がいったのか、言峰はソファーから立ち上がる。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“A mage who knew of the Holy Grail War but could not qualify as a Master.

“One man does come to mind, but no—that cannot be. The elder Makiri retired long ago.”

Apparently satisfied with his reasoning, Kotomine rises from the sofa.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“A magus who knew about the Holy Grail War but did not become a Master.
I know one such person, but that is impossible as well. The old Makiri has already retired.”
Kotomine must be satisfied, as he gets up from the sofa.

pages.ja:
「話はここまでだ。今の話を聞いては、監督役として放ってはおけん。
そのサーヴァントに関しては私が調べよう。おまえは残るランサーとの戦いに専念するがいい」
これ以上話すことはない、と言峰は出口へと歩いていく。
pages.jaRuby:
「話はここまでだ。今の話を聞いては、監督役として放ってはおけん。
そのサーヴァントに関しては私が調べよう。おまえは残るランサーとの戦いに専念するがいい」
これ以上話すことはない、と言峰は出口へと歩いていく。
pages.en:
“Our discussion is over. Now that I have heard this, I cannot ignore it in my capacity as overseer.

“I will investigate this Servant. You should devote yourself to the coming battle with Lancer.”

Having declared that there is nothing more to say, Kotomine walks toward the exit.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“This is it. I cannot let this be as a supervisor.
I shall investigate that Servant. You should concentrate on your remaining battle with Lancer.”
Kotomine walks to the exit as if there’s nothing more to talk about.

」

無言で出口へ案内する言峰を追って、この暗い石室を後にした。

…He is right. Nothing more will come of staying here.

I follow Kotomine’s silent lead and leave the dark stone chamber behind.
pages.mirrorMoon:

”
…Well, there’s certainly nothing more to be gained from being here.
I leave the dark room and follow Kotomine, who leads me to the exit silently.

pages.en:
I step out of the church.

Then, at my back—

“You understand what it means, do you not? If Saber obtains the Grail, she will die, Shirou Emiya.”

The words strike me like a demand for confirmation.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I leave the church.
Behind me,
“Saber will die once she obtains the Holy Grail. You know what that means, don’t you, Emiya Shirou?”
The priest asks as if confirming it.

」

pages.en:
“—”

From the church door above, the priest looks down upon me where I stand at the foot of the steps.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
The priest is looking down at me from the doorway.

セイバーの目的は聖杯を手に入れる事だけで、聖杯の力を欲していない。
そうして聖杯さえ手に入れば、セイバーを縛るモノはなくなる。
彼女は死の直前で此処にいる、という立場から解放され、そして
あの丘で、報われない死を迎えるだろう。

pages.en:
…If Saber obtains the Grail, she will die.

I do not need him to tell me that.

Saber wants only to possess the Grail. She has no desire to use its power.

Once she obtains it, the force binding her will be gone.

Freed from the instant before death that holds her here, she will return to that hill—and meet a death that offers her no salvation.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Saber will die if she obtains the Holy Grail.
I already know that.
Saber’s goal is to obtain the Holy Grail, and she doesn’t want the Holy Grail’s power.
Once she obtains the Holy Grail, nothing will bind her.
She will be freed from her situation, frozen on the verge of death, and
she will die an unrewarded death on that hill.

pages.ja: 「どういう風の吹き回しだ。アンタがそんな忠告をする玉か」
pages.jaRuby: 「どういう風の吹き回しだ。アンタがそんな忠告をする玉か」
pages.en: “What brought this on? You’re hardly the kind of man to offer a friendly warning.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “What’s wrong? You’re not the type to give that kind of a warning, are you?”

pages.en:
“I find the sight of you favoring Saber quite gratifying. Consider this warning an expression of my goodwill.

“Once she obtains the Grail, Saber will disappear.

“If you wish to remain with her, then you ought to abandon the Grail.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I was just happy that you are supporting Saber. I am warning you out of kindness.
Saber will disappear once she obtains the Holy Grail.
If you wish to be with her, you should give up the Holy Grail.”

pages.ja: 「……それこそ矛盾してる。聖杯がなかったらセイバーを留めておけない」
pages.jaRuby: 「……それこそ矛盾してる。聖杯がなかったらセイバーを留めておけない」
pages.en: “…That makes no sense either. Without the Grail, there’s no way to keep Saber here.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…That’s even more of a contradiction. I won’t be able to keep Saber here if I don’t have the Holy Grail.”

pages.ja: 「聖杯に頼る事はあるまい。先ほどのサーヴァントの話もある。セイバーを存命させたいのなら、魂を与え続ければいいだけではないか？」

pages.en: “You need not rely upon the Grail. Consider the Servant we just discussed. If you wish to preserve Saber’s life, you need only continue feeding her souls.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “You do not need to rely on the Holy Grail. It’s just like that Servant we were talking about. If you want to keep Saber, all you need to do is feed her souls.”

“—Go to hell. I could never do that.”

I glare at the priest.

“I see. What a pity.”

Unaffected by my stare, he smiles as though thoroughly amused.

“Even if your Servant refuses, you need only preserve a single Command Spell. That will suffice to grant your wish.”
